label: Knight army modifier
summary: The game concept Knight Army Modifier: an effect on any army that contains the acclaimed knight it belongs to.
details: The knight does not have to command the army for the effect to apply. In a text, `[knight_army_modifier|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses the singular.

label: Knight army modifier
summary: The plural name of the game concept Knight Army Modifier: effects on any army that contains a certain acclaimed knight.
details: In a text, `[knight_army_modifiers|e]` shows "Knight Army Modifiers" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the accolade texts.

label: Knight effectiveness
summary: The game concept Knight Effectiveness: how well a ruler's knights fight in battle.
details: At 100% knights fight normally; at 200% they fight as if their prowess were doubled. In a text, `[knight_effectiveness|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the marshal's council task texts.

label: Knight
summary: The icon form of the game concept Knight (a character who fights in person in an army).
details: `[knight_i]` shows the knight icon (`@knight_icon!`) instead of a word. Vanilla writes it before the knight count and in army tooltips.

label: Knight
summary: The plural name of the game concept Knight: vassals, courtiers or followers who fight in person in an army.
details: In a text, `[knights|E]` shows "Knights" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often, in achievements, buildings and other texts.

label: Knight's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Knight, shown as "Knight's" although the key is plural.
details: In a text, `[knights_possessive|E]` shows the word linked to the knight explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a message filter about a knight's tournament qualification.

label: Known tenet status
summary: The game concept Known: a tenet status meaning the rite knows a core tenet or doctrine but neither endorses nor allows practising it.
details: Such a tenet can be considered when the rite is made or split off, and its status can be raised. In a text, `[known_tenet_status|E]` shows the word "Known" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of this status and in a decision to slander a tenet.

label: Kurultai
summary: The game concept Kurultai: the council of a nomadic government.
details: Its members are the realm's elite and should be kept content or forced into obedience for a smooth succession. After a chaotic succession they may steal herd, leave the new liege and gain a claim on the realm's title. In a text, `[kurultai|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often, in council task and realm texts.

label: Kurultai member
summary: Another name of the game concept Kurultai, shown as "Kurultai Member": a member of a nomadic ruler's council.
details: In a text, `[kurultai_member|E]` shows the words linked to the kurultai explanation. Vanilla uses it in a court position requirement ("They are not a Kurultai Member").

label: Kurultai member
summary: Another name of the game concept Kurultai, shown as "Kurultai Members": the members of a nomadic ruler's council.
details: In a text, `[kurultai_members|E]` shows the words linked to the kurultai explanation. Vanilla uses it in the realm window's succession texts, about how many members are obedient.

label: Kurultai
summary: The plural name of the game concept Kurultai, shown as "Kurultais": the councils of nomadic governments.
details: In a text, `[kurultais|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in the realm window ("Disobedient kurultais").

label: Land
summary: Another name of the game concept Landed, shown as "Land": being a ruler who holds holdings.
details: Outside theocracies and republics, a commoner who gets land becomes a noble and founds a new dynasty. In a text, `[land|E]` shows the word linked to the landed explanation. Vanilla uses it in sentences like a liege giving vassals land to govern, or holding someone's de jure land.

label: Landed
summary: The game concept Landed: a ruler who holds holdings.
details: Outside theocracies and republics, a commoner who becomes landed turns noble and founds a new dynasty. In a text, `[landed|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often (over 100 uses), for example "a landed title" or "a landed spouse".

label: Language
summary: The game concept Language: the culture pillar that sets which language a culture's people speak.
details: Cultures that share a language get a lasting bonus to cultural acceptance. A character can know several languages; knowing one halves the cultural acceptance opinion penalty towards characters and counties that speak it, and discourages independence and claimant factions. In a text, `[language|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Foreign language limit
summary: The game concept Foreign Language Limit: how many languages a character can comfortably remember.
details: Going over it means forgetting a language or suffering stress; the language of their own culture does not count. Everyone starts at 1, and it rises with learning (one per set number of points) and other sources, such as a perk. In a text, `[language_limit|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the learn language scheme texts.

label: Language
summary: The plural name of the game concept Language: what the people of cultures speak, and what characters can learn.
details: In a text, `[languages|E]` shows "Languages" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for the number of known languages, in council task and court position texts.

label: Law
summary: The game concept Law: the rules that set how a realm is structured.
details: The most basic ones are the government authority laws, which set how lieges and vassals deal with each other; succession and title laws matter for who inherits. In a text, `[law|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often (over 100 uses), for example "Adopts the ... law".

label: Law
summary: The icon form of the game concept Law (the rules that structure a realm).
details: `[law_i]` shows the law icon (`@law_icon!`) instead of a word. Vanilla puts it right before `[law|E]`, after a law's name.

label: Law
summary: The plural name of the game concept Law: the rules that set how a realm is structured.
details: In a text, `[laws|E]` shows "Laws" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in AI personality texts and other concept explanations.

label: Leading house
summary: The game concept Leading House: the house that is the agreed leader of a house bloc.
details: In a text, `[leading_house|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in decisions about which house leads a confederation.

label: Leading house's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Leading House (the agreed leader of a house bloc).
details: In a text, `[leading_house_possessive|E]` shows "Leading House's" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in house bloc texts, such as the leading house's aspiration. A use like `[leading_house.GetHouse...]` is a different thing: it reads a saved value named `leading_house`.

label: Leading house
summary: The plural name of the game concept Leading House: the agreed leaders of house blocs.
details: In a text, `[leading_houses|E]` shows "Leading Houses" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the bloc supremacy war's explanation and a bloc transfer rule.

label: Learning
summary: Another name of the game concept Learning Skill, shown as "Learning": the skill for a character's literacy and wisdom.
details: A ruler's learning affects the cost of raising crown authority and gives some piety each month. In a text, `[learning|E]` shows the word linked to the skill's explanation. Vanilla uses it often (about 250 uses), for example in board game events.

label: Learning
summary: The icon form of the game concept Learning Skill (a character's literacy and wisdom).
details: `[learning_i]` shows the learning skill icon (`@skill_learning_icon!`) instead of a word. Vanilla puts it right before `[learning|E]` or `[learning_skill|E]`, for example in council task texts.

label: Learning lifestyle
summary: The game concept Learning Lifestyle: the lifestyle for characters who want a long and healthy life, piety, or more bonuses from their faith.
details: In a text, `[learning_lifestyle|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts about gaining learning lifestyle experience.

label: Learning lifestyle
summary: The icon form of the game concept Learning Lifestyle.
details: `[learning_lifestyle_i]` shows the learning lifestyle icon (`@learning_lifestyle_icon!`) instead of a word. Vanilla uses it once, in a bookmark character's description.

label: Learning skill
summary: The game concept Learning Skill: the skill for a character's literacy and wisdom.
details: A ruler's learning affects the cost of raising crown authority and gives some piety each month; characters with high learning know theology, philosophy, languages and mathematics. In a text, `[learning_skill|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in council task texts.

label: Learning contract
summary: The game concept Learning Contract: a task contract, typically about copying texts or helping with acts of solidarity.
details: In a text, `[learning_task_contract|E]` shows "Learning Contract" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Learning contract's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Learning Contract (a task contract about copying texts and the like).
details: In a text, `[learning_task_contract_possessive|E]` shows "Learning Contract's" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Learning contract
summary: The plural name of the game concept Learning Contract: task contracts about copying texts or helping with acts of solidarity.
details: In a text, `[learning_task_contracts|E]` shows "Learning Contracts" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a decision event that creates such contracts on the map.

label: Learning contracts'
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Learning Contract (task contracts about copying texts and the like).
details: In a text, `[learning_task_contracts_possessive|E]` shows "Learning Contracts'" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Lease
summary: Another name of the game concept Leasing, shown as "Lease": handing minor baronies over to holy orders or clergy.
details: A leased barony gives its taxes and levies to the lessee instead of the holder, but stays part of the holder's realm; county capitals cannot be leased. In a text, `[lease|E]` shows the word linked to the leasing explanation. Vanilla uses it in decisions about monastic orders and in the explanation of realm priests.

label: Lease contract
summary: The game concept Lease Contract: the legal terms under which a character leases a title.
details: It also decides who their religious superior is. In a text, `[lease_contract|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the leasing explanation and the character window.

label: Leasing
summary: Another name of the game concept Leasing, shown as "Leased": a minor barony handed over to a holy order or clergy.
details: Its taxes and levies go to the lessee instead of the holder. In a text, `[leased|E]` shows the word linked to the leasing explanation. Vanilla uses it in decisions that need a barony that is not leased.

label: Leasing
summary: Another name of the game concept Leasing, shown as "Leases": baronies handed over to holy orders or clergy.
details: In a text, `[leases|E]` shows the word linked to the leasing explanation. Vanilla uses it in decisions that count or transfer a monastic order's leases.

label: Leasing
summary: The game concept Leasing: handing minor baronies over to holy orders, monastic orders or clergy.
details: A leased barony gives its taxes and levies to the lessee instead of the holder, but stays part of the holder's realm; county capitals cannot be leased. Military orders lease castles and cities, while monastic orders and clergy lease temples. In a text, `[leasing|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Legalism
summary: The game concept Legalism: a core tenet that stresses legal practice and tradition in theology and devotion.
details: It affects the cost of laws, and whether vassals join factions depending on how many sins or virtues their ruler has. In a text, `[legalism|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Legalism
summary: Another name of the game concept Legalism, shown as "Legalistic": a core tenet that stresses legal practice and tradition.
details: In a text, `[legalistic|E]` shows the word linked to the legalism explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Legend
summary: The game concept Legend: the great deeds of a character's life, built up from a legend seed.
details: Legends give legitimacy and can also give skills, opinion, dynasty prestige, prestige or piety; baronies the legend has spread to can get extra effects if its owner or a promoter holds them. In a text, `[legend|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often, in court position and decision texts.

label: Famed legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Legend Quality, shown as "Famed": the first of a legend's three quality levels.
details: A legend is Famed, Illustrious or Mythical; quality sets how strong it is and how far it spreads, and rises by spreading to more baronies and paying an upgrade cost. In a text, `[legend_famed|E]` shows the word linked to the quality explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the Famed quality.

label: Heroic legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Legend Type, shown as "Heroic Legend": the legend type that grants prestige.
details: A legend is Legitimizing, Heroic or Holy, and the type sets which kind of rewards and content it has. In a text, `[legend_heroic|E]` shows the words linked to the legend type explanation. Vanilla uses it in a legacy text about completing a mythical heroic legend.

label: Holy legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Legend Type, shown as "Holy Legend": the legend type that grants piety.
details: A legend is Legitimizing, Heroic or Holy, and the type sets which kind of rewards and content it has. In a text, `[legend_holy|E]` shows the words linked to the legend type explanation. Vanilla uses it in a legacy text about completing a mythical holy legend.

label: Legend
summary: The icon form of the game concept Legend (the great deeds of a character's life).
details: `[legend_i]` shows the legend icon (`@legend_icon!`) instead of a word. Vanilla uses it as the prefix in front of legend modifiers' names.

label: Illustrious legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Legend Quality, shown as "Illustrious": the middle of a legend's three quality levels.
details: A legend is Famed, Illustrious or Mythical; a higher quality means stronger effects and a wider spread. In a text, `[legend_illustrious|E]` shows the word linked to the quality explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the Illustrious quality.

label: Legitimizing legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Legend Type, shown as "Legitimizing Legend": the legend type that grants legitimacy.
details: A legend is Legitimizing, Heroic or Holy, and the type sets which kind of rewards and content it has. In a text, `[legend_legitimizing|E]` shows the words linked to the legend type explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Legend library
summary: The game concept Legend Library: where a ruler keeps completed legends that spread to their domain, that they created, or that they promoted.
details: While travelling through a legend's spread area you can add it yourself, and you can remove legends at any time. In a text, `[legend_library|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a message when a legend is added.

label: Mythical legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Legend Quality, shown as "Mythical": the highest of a legend's three quality levels.
details: A legend is Famed, Illustrious or Mythical; a higher quality means stronger effects and a wider spread. In a text, `[legend_mythical|E]` shows the word linked to the quality explanation. Vanilla uses it in legacy texts about completing a mythical legend.

label: Legend promoter
summary: The game concept Legend Promoter: a ruler who supports another ruler's legend.
details: The promoter pays a monthly gold contribution and gets extra bonuses that depend on the legend's type and quality. In a text, `[legend_promoter|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the legend texts, such as the promoter's modifiers.

label: Legend promoter
summary: The plural name of the game concept Legend Promoter: rulers who support another ruler's legend.
details: In a text, `[legend_promoters|E]` shows "Legend Promoters" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the legend explanations, about their monthly contribution.

label: Legend protagonist
summary: The game concept Legend Protagonist: the main character of a legend, whose deeds it tells.
details: This can be the legend's owner or any family member, dead or alive, who is at least 16. They get no direct bonus themselves, but the legend's content is about them. In a text, `[legend_protagonist|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Many vanilla lines like `[legend_protagonist.GetTitledFirstName]` are a different thing: they use a saved character named `legend_protagonist`.

label: Legend protagonist
summary: The plural name of the game concept Legend Protagonist: the main characters of legends.
details: In a text, `[legend_protagonists|E]` shows "Legend Protagonists" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a tutorial text about choosing who a legend is about.

label: Legend quality
summary: The game concept Legend Quality: how strong a legend's effects are and how far it spreads.
details: It also affects the final rewards. The levels are Famed, Illustrious and Mythical; quality rises by spreading the legend to more baronies and paying an upgrade cost, and it is kept when the owner dies and their family carries on. In a text, `[legend_quality|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Legend seed
summary: The game concept Legend Seed: a legend in the making, which a ruler can found to start a legend.
details: Seeds come from certain conditions, such as being the heir of Charlemagne, or from great deeds: major decisions, winning a great holy war, becoming king or emperor, holding a grand activity, hunting a legendary animal and more. In a text, `[legend_seed|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in court position texts and a message filter.

label: Legend seed
summary: The plural name of the game concept Legend Seed: legends in the making that a ruler can found.
details: In a text, `[legend_seeds|E]` shows "Legend Seeds" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the legend explanation and the legends window.

label: Legend type
summary: The game concept Legend Type: the kind of a legend, which sets its rewards and the theme of its content.
details: The types are Legitimizing, Heroic and Holy, which grant legitimacy, prestige and piety. In a text, `[legend_type|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the legend and legend promoter explanations.

label: Legend type
summary: The plural name of the game concept Legend Type: the kinds of legends (Legitimizing, Heroic, Holy).
details: In a text, `[legend_types|E]` shows "Legend Types" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name in a link.

label: Legend
summary: The plural name of the game concept Legend: the great deeds of characters' lives.
details: In a text, `[legends|E]` shows "Legends" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in personality texts about who likes to create and promote which kind of legend.

label: Legitimacy
summary: The game concept Legitimacy: a ruler's right to reign, as a value.
details: Only rulers have it; it is set when they become ruler (their initial legitimacy), and part of it passes to their heir. Vassals expect a certain level from their liege, and it affects many game systems. In a text, `[legitimacy|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it very often (about 280 uses).

label: Legitimacy expectations
summary: Another name of the game concept Expected Legitimacy, shown as "Legitimacy Expectations": the legitimacy level vassals expect from their ruler.
details: It depends on their shared history; it is lower, for example, when the ruler is the vassal's de jure liege, close family, preferred heir, or of a dynasty the vassal has served for over 50 years. In a text, `[legitimacy_expectations|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the legitimacy and heir explanations.

label: Legitimacy level
summary: Another name of the game concept Legitimacy Level, shown as "Legitimacy Gain": the steps of a ruler's legitimacy.
details: Legitimacy is gained by winning wars, releasing valuable prisoners, creating legends, holding court or attending activities, and lost through epidemics in the capital, lost wars, lost titles or an exposed hostile scheme, among others. In a text, `[legitimacy_gain|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Legitimacy
summary: The icon form of the game concept Legitimacy (a ruler's right to reign).
details: `[legitimacy_i]` shows a legitimacy icon instead of a word; its text calls `GetLocalPlayerLegitimacyTextIcon`, so the icon follows the local player's legitimacy. Vanilla puts it before a number in effect texts ("You gain ... legitimacy").

label: Legitimacy level
summary: The game concept Legitimacy Level: the steps of a ruler's legitimacy, which rise and fall with what they do.
details: There are typically five levels above an illegitimate bottom level. They are gained by winning wars, releasing valuable prisoners, creating legends, holding court or attending activities, and lost through epidemics in the capital, lost wars, lost titles or an exposed hostile scheme. In a text, `[legitimacy_level|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Legitimacy level
summary: The plural name of the game concept Legitimacy Level: the steps of a ruler's legitimacy.
details: In a text, `[legitimacy_levels|E]` shows "Legitimacy Levels" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the legitimacy explanation and in a warning that a ruler is below a vassal's expectations.

label: Legitimate
summary: The game concept Legitimate: a child born to married parents, as opposed to a bastard, who cannot inherit titles.
details: Children of concubines also count as legitimate, though of slightly lower standing. In a text, `[legitimate|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the spouse and concubine explanations.

label: Legitimized bastard
summary: Another name of the game concept Legitimized Bastard, shown as "Legitimized": a bastard declared legitimate.
details: It can happen at birth or later through a character interaction, if their house head agrees. They inherit like legitimate children but keep the stain of bastardy. In a text, `[legitimized|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in faith texts about whether a rite allows bastards to be legitimized.

label: Legitimized bastard
summary: The game concept Legitimized Bastard: a bastard who has been declared legitimate, at birth or later.
details: Later legitimization goes through a character interaction and needs the house head's approval. They have the same inheritance rights as legitimate children, but the stain of bastardy stays with them. In a text, `[legitimized_bastard|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in relation and bastard interaction texts.

label: Lessee
summary: Another name of the game concept Leasing, shown as "Lessee": the holy order or clergy who leases a barony and gets its taxes and levies.
details: In a text, `[lessee|E]` shows the word linked to the leasing explanation. Vanilla uses it in the leasing explanation and in the holding tooltip, next to the lessee's name.

label: Levy
summary: The game concept Levies: the poorly armed fighters who make up most of an army.
details: Each holding gives a set number of levies to its holder, and vassals pass part of theirs to their liege. They are mostly peasant militias, ruffians and the like, and count as a unit type of their own. In a text, `[levies|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often (about 180 uses).

label: Levy
summary: Another name of the game concept Levies, shown as "Levy": one of the poorly armed fighters who make up most of an army.
details: In a text, `[levy|E]` shows the word linked to the levies explanation. Vanilla uses it in council task texts (levy reinforcement rate) and in the explanation of a levy soldier's strength.

label: Liberty faction
summary: The game concept Liberty Faction: a faction of vassals who want to lower the government authority and, where they have one, ease their own vassal contract.
details: If it wins, the liege cannot change the realm's government authority for some time. In a text, `[liberty_faction|E]` shows "Liberty Faction" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the authority explanations and the war's outcome text.

label: Liberty faction
summary: The plural name of the game concept Liberty Faction: factions that want to lower the government authority.
details: In a text, `[liberty_factions|E]` shows "Liberty Factions" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in an effect that makes vassals less likely to join claimant and liberty factions.

label: Liege
summary: The game concept Liege: a ruler with at least one vassal.
details: A liege can in turn be the vassal of a higher-ranked ruler, and so on. In a text, `[liege|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it very often (over 1200 uses).

label: Liege's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Liege (a ruler with at least one vassal).
details: In a text, `[liege_possessive|E]` shows "Liege's" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in building and core texts, such as "Liege's faith".

label: Liege taxes
summary: The game concept Liege Taxes: the taxes a vassal must pay their liege as part of their obligations.
details: An independent ruler pays none. From the liege's side the same taxes are called vassal taxes. In a text, `[liege_taxes|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the tax explanations.

label: Liege
summary: The plural name of the game concept Liege: rulers with at least one vassal.
details: In a text, `[lieges|E]` shows "Lieges" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the law and alliance explanations.

label: Life expectancy
summary: The game concept Life Expectancy: how many years a character is expected to live before dying of natural causes.
details: A high life expectancy also makes characters visibly age more slowly. In a text, `[life_expectancy|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in the name of the life expectancy modifier (in years).

label: Lifestyle
summary: The game concept Lifestyle: a way of life an adult ruler chooses, which lets them pick a focus and earn perks.
details: Each lifestyle has its own kind of experience, which buys that lifestyle's perks. In a text, `[lifestyle|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in achievements and other concept explanations.

label: Lifestyle experience
summary: The game concept Lifestyle Experience: points a character gathers in a lifestyle to earn its perks.
details: It builds up by itself while a focus is selected, or comes from events; there is one kind per lifestyle, and enough of it earns a perk. In a text, `[lifestyle_experience|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the adult education activity texts.

label: Lifestyle trait
summary: The game concept Lifestyle Trait: a trait gained from certain lifestyle perks, decisions or interactions.
details: Some can be upgraded as the character gets better at the skill, with levels 1 to 3 shown as stars on the icon. In a text, `[lifestyle_trait|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in activity texts, such as the hunt.

label: Lifestyle trait
summary: The plural name of the game concept Lifestyle Trait: traits gained from lifestyle perks, decisions or interactions.
details: In a text, `[lifestyle_traits|E]` shows "Lifestyle Traits" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in learning contract events.

label: Lifestyle
summary: The plural name of the game concept Lifestyle: the ways of life adult rulers can choose.
details: In a text, `[lifestyles|E]` shows "Lifestyles" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a natural disaster contract's rewards.

label: Light cavalry
summary: The game concept Light Cavalry: mounted men-at-arms who are good at scouting and chasing the enemy.
details: They generally counter archers and are countered by spearmen, are often strong on flat terrain, and are usually better than heavy cavalry at pursuit and screen. In a text, `[light_cavalry|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the other unit types' explanations.

label: Limited crown authority
summary: Another name of the game concept Limited Crown Authority, shown as "Limited": the second-lowest level of crown authority.
details: At this level vassals have -10 opinion of their liege, the liege may revoke titles and take away a vassal's vassals, and the ruler can switch between the available partition succession laws. In a text, `[limited|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the crown authority explanations.

label: Limited crown authority
summary: The game concept Limited Crown Authority: the second-lowest level of crown authority.
details: Vassals have -10 opinion of their liege, the liege may revoke titles and take away a vassal's vassals, and the ruler can switch between the available partition succession laws. In a text, `[limited_crown_authority|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the revoke and higher authority explanations.

label: Limited nomadic authority
summary: The game concept Limited (nomadic authority): the second-lowest level of nomadic authority.
details: At this level migration can target de jure duchies within the Great Steppe, titles can be revoked, the liege may imprison characters in their realm, and a decision to step away from the steppe becomes usable. In a text, `[limited_nomadic|E]` shows the word "Limited" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in the nomadic authority explanation.

label: Limited tribal authority
summary: Another name of the game concept Limited Tribal Authority, shown as "Limited": the second-lowest level of tribal authority.
details: At this level vassals have -10 opinion of their liege, and the liege may imprison characters in their realm. In a text, `[limited_tribal|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the tribal authority explanations.

label: Limited tribal authority
summary: The game concept Limited Tribal Authority: the second-lowest level of tribal authority.
details: Vassals have -10 opinion of their liege, and the liege may imprison characters in their realm. In a text, `[limited_tribal_authority|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this exact name.

label: Line of succession
summary: Another name of the game concept Line of Succession, shown as "Line": the order in which characters stand to inherit titles.
details: The succession law sets the order. In a text, `[line|E]` shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in phrases like "You are 2nd in line for ..." and "the next candidate in line".

label: Line of succession
summary: The game concept Line of Succession: the order in which certain characters stand to inherit certain titles.
details: The order is set by the succession law. In a text, `[line_of_succession|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in court position and dynasty texts.

label: Local arbitration
summary: The game concept Local Arbitration: a decision that lets a character improve the county they are in.
details: The word shown is the decision's name, "Local Arbitration". In a text, `[local_arbitration|E]` shows it linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a perk that unlocks the decision.

label: Local arbitration
summary: Another name of the game concept Local Arbitration, shown as "Local Arbitration Decision": a decision to improve the county a character is in.
details: In a text, `[local_arbitration_decision|E]` shows the words linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes `[local_arbitration|E]`.

label: Locales
summary: The game concept Locales: the places a guest can visit at a tournament while its contests are being prepared.
details: Writing `[locale|E]` in a text shows the word (its name text is the plural "Locales") linked to the concept's explanation. Each locale offers chances to socialize with other guests, improve one's progress to victory, or sabotage contestants; a guest who picks none is sent to a random one after a short while. The game's texts use the form `locales` instead of this one.

label: Locales
summary: The game concept Locales, in its plural form: the places a guest can visit at a tournament while its contests are being prepared.
details: Writing `[locales|E]` in a text shows the word "Locales" linked to the concept's explanation. Each locale offers chances to socialize, improve one's progress to victory, or sabotage contestants. Vanilla uses it in the tournament texts, for example telling the player to visit locales to improve their chances.

label: Location
summary: The game concept Location: the place in the world where a character currently is.
details: Writing `[location|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Every character has a location, and getting from one location to another means travelling. Vanilla uses it in activity texts (the host holds an activity in a location everyone must travel to) and in a wanderer focus text about stress loss.

label: Long reign
summary: The game concept Long Reign: an opinion bonus that everyone in a realm gets towards a liege who has ruled them for a long time, growing over the years.
details: Writing `[long_reign|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Its counterpart is the short reign penalty, which new lieges suffer and which fades over time. Vanilla uses it as the name of the long reign opinion line and in a demand-submission text.

label: Loot
summary: The game concept Loot: the gold an attacker gets from a holding by raiding it, occupying it in a siege, or bartering with it.
details: Writing `[loot|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The more prosperous a holding is, the more loot it has; a holding that was raided, besieged or bartered with recently has none. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that add loot to an army and in a council task's tooltip.

label: Loot icon
summary: The game concept Loot (the gold taken from a raided, besieged or bartered holding), in its icon form.
details: This is another name of the loot concept whose name text is the loot icon, so `[loot_i|E]` shows that icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it as `[loot_i]`, without the link, to put the plain icon in front of loot numbers in a council task's tooltip.

label: Lover
summary: The game concept Lover: a relation between two characters who are in an ongoing romantic and sexual affair.
details: Writing `[lover|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Lovers are often not married to each other, so most lover relations begin as secrets. A woman can become pregnant by a man who is her lover. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as becoming someone's lover.

label: Lover's
summary: The game concept Lover (a relation between two characters in an ongoing affair), in its possessive form "Lover's".
details: Writing `[lover_possessive|E]` in a text shows "Lover's" linked to the lover concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an achievement text (murder your lover's spouse).

label: Lovers
summary: The game concept Lover (a relation between two characters in an ongoing affair), in its plural form "Lovers".
details: Writing `[lovers|E]` in a text shows "Lovers" linked to the lover concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as two characters becoming lovers.

label: Lovers'
summary: The game concept Lover (a relation between two characters in an ongoing affair), in its plural possessive form "Lovers'".
details: Writing `[lovers_possessive|E]` in a text shows "Lovers'" linked to the lover concept's explanation. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Lowborn
summary: The game concept Commoner, under its other name "Lowborn": a character who is not a member of a noble dynasty.
details: Writing `[lowborn|E]` in a text shows the word "Lowborn" linked to the commoner concept's explanation. Commoners can still be powerful rulers of theocracies and republics. A commoner who becomes landed turns noble and founds a dynasty of their own, except in republics and theocracies, which are mostly run by commoners. Vanilla uses it in an achievement and a building's condition text.

label: Main phase
summary: The game concept Main Phase: the part of a battle in which the soldiers and knights of both sides fight each other.
details: Writing `[main_phase|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. It follows the maneuver phase and ends when one side has lost all its troops as casualties or has retreated; then the battle enters the aftermath. Vanilla uses it in the combat window's tooltip for the current combat phase.

label: Mainline rite
summary: The game concept Mainline Rite: the rite holding the most prominent set of beliefs of a faith.
details: Writing `[mainline_rite|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Every other rite of the faith counts as divergent from it. If the faith has a head of faith, the mainline rite is the one they follow, so it can change when a successor of another rite takes over. Vanilla uses it in decision requirements and in the faith and heresy concept texts.

label: Mainline
summary: The game concept Mainline Rite (the rite holding a faith's most prominent beliefs), in its short form "Mainline".
details: Writing `[mainline_rite_short|E]` in a text shows the word "Mainline" linked to the mainline rite concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the Christian church window, in front of the faith's adjective and the word rite.

label: Mainline rites
summary: The game concept Mainline Rite (the rite holding a faith's most prominent beliefs), in its plural form "Mainline Rites".
details: Writing `[mainline_rites|E]` in a text shows "Mainline Rites" linked to the mainline rite concept's explanation. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Majesty tour
summary: The game concept Majesty Tour: a type of tour in which the ruler tries to win over their vassals by raising their opinion.
details: Writing `[majesty_tour|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla's tutorial text says each stop of a majesty tour raises the opinion of the vassal visited there; the other tour types are the intimidation and taxation tours.

label: Manage Royal Guards
summary: The game concept Manage Royal Guards: a councillor task of the marshal that makes knights more effective and makes hostile schemes against the marshal's liege less likely to succeed.
details: Writing `[manage_guards|E]` in a text shows the task's name, "Manage Royal Guards", linked to the concept's explanation. The game's description begins with the name of the Increase Control task instead of this one, but the rest describes this task. Vanilla's royal court texts say a court grandeur level unlocks it.

label: Mandala
summary: The game concept Mandala: a form of government whose rulers have a small domain and few direct vassals and grow their realm through tributaries instead.
details: Writing `[mandala|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A mandala ruler can aim to be seen as a god king (Devaraja) and then relies on mandala radiance to win and keep tributaries. The ruler has to keep up their tributaries' opinion and relations with them to keep them. Vanilla uses it in piety level and government texts.

label: Mandala aspect
summary: The game concept Mandala Aspect: one of the divine aspects a mandala ruler aligns with on the way to being revered as a god.
details: Writing `[mandala_aspect|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The aspects are Creation, Serenity, Destruction and Trickery, and the chosen one shapes what is expected of the ruler and what they do. Vanilla's texts speak of a house assuming an aspect.

label: Mandala aspects
summary: The game concept Mandala Aspect (a divine aspect a mandala ruler aligns with), in its plural form "Mandala Aspects".
details: Writing `[mandala_aspects|E]` in a text shows "Mandala Aspects" linked to the concept's explanation. The aspects are Creation, Serenity, Destruction and Trickery. Vanilla uses it in a government's feature list (uses mandala aspects).

label: Mandala decree
summary: The game concept Mandala Decree: one of the three decrees with which a mandala ruler sets the direction of their realm.
details: Writing `[mandala_decree|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The three are the Prosperity, Expansion and Reverence decrees. A mandala realm is very centralized: the ruler holds power over subjects and laws and can change them with little objection. Vanilla's texts speak of selecting a decree.

label: Expansion decree
summary: The game concept Expansion Decree: the mandala decree that has all subjects work on expanding the realm.
details: Writing `[mandala_decree_expansion|E]` in a text shows the decree's name linked to the concept's explanation. Under it, more soldiers, military accommodations and support for the ruler's wars come first. The decree is a law of the same key. None of the game's texts use this concept link.

label: Prosperity decree
summary: The game concept Prosperity Decree: the mandala decree that has all subjects work on building up the realm.
details: Writing `[mandala_decree_prosperity|E]` in a text shows the decree's name linked to the concept's explanation. Under it, efforts go into development, buildings, gathering wealth and personal relations. The decree is a law of the same key. None of the game's texts use this concept link.

label: Reverence decree
summary: The game concept Reverence Decree: the mandala decree that has all subjects focus on spirituality and worship.
details: Writing `[mandala_decree_reverence|E]` in a text shows the decree's name linked to the concept's explanation. Pilgrimages, rituals and piety are at its heart. The decree is a law of the same key. None of the game's texts use this concept link.

label: Mandala decrees
summary: The game concept Mandala Decree (one of the three decrees that set a mandala realm's direction), in its plural form "Mandala Decrees".
details: Writing `[mandala_decrees|E]` in a text shows "Mandala Decrees" linked to the concept's explanation. The three are the Prosperity, Expansion and Reverence decrees. Vanilla uses it in a government's feature list (uses mandala decrees).

label: Mandala government
summary: The game concept Mandala, under its other name "Mandala Government": a form of government that grows its realm through tributaries rather than a large domain.
details: Writing `[mandala_government|E]` in a text shows "Mandala Government" linked to the mandala concept's explanation. Mandala rulers have a limited domain and few direct vassals, can aim to be a god king, and depend on mandala radiance and their tributaries' opinion. Vanilla uses it in texts about converting to this government.

label: Mandala icon
summary: The game concept Mandala (a government form that grows through tributaries), in its icon form.
details: This is another name of the mandala concept whose name text is the mandala government icon, so `[mandala_i|E]` shows that icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla puts it in front of the word mandala in opinion modifier names.

label: Mandala radiance
summary: The game concept Mandala Radiance: how strongly a mandala ruler draws in and holds on to subjects.
details: Writing `[mandala_radiance|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. It combines the ruler's level of devotion (piety level), the level of the mandala capital great building and the level of their mandala aspect; more radiance brings bigger rewards and more subjects. Vanilla shows it in the character window against a maximum set by a define.

label: Mandala ritual
summary: The game concept Mandala Ritual: a task that appears now and then for a mandala ruler, showing that a part of the realm needs their guidance.
details: Writing `[mandala_ritual|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The more skilled the ruler is in their mandala aspect, the more they gain from appearing for their subjects. Vanilla's texts say a ritual appears in a province and asks for the ruler's presence.

label: Mandala ritual tier
summary: The game concept Mandala Ritual Tier: how much a mandala ritual's destination would gain from the ruler's visit, and how big the ruler's own rewards are.
details: Writing `[mandala_ritual_tier|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the label of a ritual's tier.

label: Mandala rituals
summary: The game concept Mandala Ritual (a task that appears for a mandala ruler where the realm needs guidance), in its plural form "Mandala Rituals".
details: Writing `[mandala_rituals|E]` in a text shows "Mandala Rituals" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla's texts say the realm's provinces and subjects now and then spawn mandala rituals, and a cultural tradition raises the piety and legitimacy they give.

label: Devaraja successor
summary: The game concept Mandala Succession, under its other name "Devaraja Successor": the trials a mandala ruler's heir faces to prove they are a worthy successor.
details: Writing `[mandala_succesor|E]` (the key is spelled this way) shows "Devaraja Successor" linked to the mandala succession concept's explanation. When a mandala ruler who chose an aspect dies, the heir faces skill challenges in that aspect's skill and two other aspect skills; passing keeps the realm stable, failing brings growing penalties. Vanilla's mandala text says tributaries may scatter unless the ruler is a worthy successor.

label: Mandala succession
summary: The game concept Mandala Succession: the trials the heir of a mandala ruler faces after that ruler dies.
details: Writing `[mandala_succession|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. It applies when the dead ruler had chosen a mandala aspect: the heir faces skill challenges in that aspect's skill and two other aspect skills. Passing convinces their followers and keeps the realm stable; failing brings growing penalties. Vanilla's texts say the trials wait until the heir returns to their capital or becomes an adult, and that failing them can cost the primary title.

label: Succession
summary: The game concept Mandala Succession, under its short name "Succession": the trials a mandala ruler's heir faces after the ruler dies.
details: Writing `[mandala_succession_succession|E]` in a text shows the word "Succession" linked to the mandala succession concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it after the word mandala, for example in dynasty legacy and aspect texts that let an heir skip one of the challenges.

label: Mandala trials
summary: The game concept Mandala Succession, under its other name "Mandala Trials": the trials a mandala ruler's heir faces to keep the realm.
details: Writing `[mandala_trials|E]` in a text shows "Mandala Trials" linked to the mandala succession concept's explanation. The heir faces skill challenges in the aspect's skill and two other aspect skills; failing brings growing penalties. Vanilla's succession law text says the new ruler must pass them to keep the whole realm and its tributaries.

label: Mandalas
summary: The game concept Mandala (a government form that grows through tributaries), in its plural form "Mandalas".
details: Writing `[mandalas|E]` in a text shows "Mandalas" linked to the mandala concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a modifier text saying mandalas prefer to be tributaries.

label: Mandate
summary: The game concept Mandate: a task a liege who shares power sets for their diarch, from which the liege slowly gains benefits.
details: Writing `[mandate|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. It works much like a councillor task. A diarch who does the job well both tips the scales of power towards themselves and causes strife with the other vassals. Vanilla uses it in effect texts about a liege setting a diarch's mandate.

label: Mandate of Heaven
summary: The game concept Mandate of Heaven: a special kind of legitimacy that only the Son of Heaven has, standing for their right to rule all under heaven.
details: Writing `[mandate_of_heaven|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. It is tied closely to the dynastic cycle: the cycle changes how the emperor gains legitimacy, and the mandate's level can move the cycle to another phase. Vanilla uses it in the name of the legitimacy type's ranks.

label: Mandate
summary: The game concept Mandate of Heaven (the Son of Heaven's special legitimacy), in its short form "Mandate".
details: Writing `[mandate_of_heaven_mandate|E]` in a text shows the word "Mandate" linked to the Mandate of Heaven concept's explanation, not to the diarchy mandate. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Mandate's
summary: The game concept Mandate (a task a liege sets for their diarch), in its possessive form "Mandate's".
details: Writing `[mandate_possessive|E]` in a text shows "Mandate's" linked to the mandate concept's explanation. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Mandates
summary: The game concept Mandate (a task a liege sets for their diarch), in its plural form "Mandates".
details: Writing `[mandates|E]` in a text shows "Mandates" linked to the mandate concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as a heading in the diarchy window and in the diarchy concept text.

label: Mandates'
summary: The game concept Mandate (a task a liege sets for their diarch), in its plural possessive form "Mandates'".
details: Writing `[mandates_possessive|E]` in a text shows "Mandates'" linked to the mandate concept's explanation. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Maneuver
summary: The game concept Maneuver: the opening phase of a battle, the time before the main phase when the armies begin fighting.
details: Writing `[maneuver|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A battle has three phases: maneuver, main phase and aftermath. Vanilla uses it in the combat window's tooltip for the current combat phase.

label: Manipulation
summary: The game concept Manipulation: a kind of hook gained by manipulating another character's mind so they do what you want.
details: Writing `[manipulation|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A hook is a hold over a character that can make them do things. None of the game's texts use this concept link.

label: Manor
summary: The game concept Japanese Manor, under its name "Manor": a domicile held by the house head of a notable noble family in the Japanese realms, a private landholding not tied to any landed title.
details: Writing `[manor|E]` in a text shows the word "Manor" linked to the Japanese manor concept's explanation. Manor buildings can be built in it to add to the family's wealth and influence. Vanilla uses it in government features, AI reasons and an interaction text about raiding a house's manor.

label: Manor building
summary: The game concept Japanese Manor Building, under its name "Manor Building": a lasting improvement built in a Japanese manor.
details: Writing `[manor_building|E]` in a text shows "Manor Building" linked to the concept's explanation. The manor's owner can build many kinds of them to earn private income, grow the family's influence and unlock decisions, interactions and more. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Manor buildings
summary: The game concept Japanese Manor Building (a lasting improvement built in a Japanese manor), in its plural form "Manor Buildings".
details: Writing `[manor_buildings|E]` in a text shows "Manor Buildings" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the heading of the Japanese manor's buildings.

label: Manors
summary: The game concept Japanese Manor (a noble house head's private landholding in the Japanese realms), in its plural form "Manors".
details: Writing `[manors|E]` in a text shows "Manors" linked to the Japanese manor concept's explanation. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Mansion
summary: The game concept East Asian Mansion, under its name "Mansion": a domicile held by the house head of a notable noble family, a private landholding not tied to any landed title.
details: Writing `[mansion|E]` in a text shows the word "Mansion" linked to the concept's explanation. Buildings can be built in it to add to the family's wealth and influence, and future generations inherit it. The game's description names the Japanese governments, the same text as the Japanese manor's. Vanilla uses it in government features and dynasty legacies that unlock mansion buildings.

label: Mansions
summary: The game concept East Asian Mansion (a noble house head's private landholding), in its plural form "Mansions".
details: Writing `[mansions|E]` in a text shows "Mansions" linked to the mansion concept's explanation. None of the game's texts use this form.

label: Marriage
summary: The game concept Marriage: a union between two spouses, and with betrothals the main way to form an alliance with another ruler.
details: Writing `[marriage|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Spouses can have legitimate children, who can be bred and raised as heirs. A marriage ends only when one spouse dies or divorces the other. Vanilla uses it in council and marriage acceptance texts.

label: Marriages
summary: The game concept Marriage (a union of two spouses, a main way to form alliances), in its plural form "Marriages".
details: Writing `[marriages|E]` in a text shows "Marriages" linked to the marriage concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts about breeding, arranging marriages for family members and government rules.

label: Married
summary: The game concept Marriage (a union of two spouses), as the word "Married".
details: Writing `[married|E]` in a text shows "Married" linked to the marriage concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the past-tense texts of the marry effect (married someone).

label: Marries
summary: The game concept Marriage (a union of two spouses), as the word "Marries".
details: Writing `[marries|E]` in a text shows "Marries" linked to the marriage concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the marry effect's texts and in a message filter for a close family member marrying.

label: Marry
summary: The game concept Marriage (a union of two spouses), as the word "Marry".
details: Writing `[marry|E]` in a text shows "Marry" linked to the marriage concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an achievement and in AI personality descriptions.

label: Marrying
summary: The game concept Marriage (a union of two spouses), as the word "Marrying".
details: Writing `[marrying|E]` in a text shows "Marrying" linked to the marriage concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in tutorial texts about allying without marrying.

label: Marshal
summary: The game concept Marshal: the councillor in charge of military matters and the ruler's chief commander.
details: Writing `[marshal|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in council texts, for example the warning that the ruler has no marshal.

label: Marshals
summary: The game concept Marshal (the councillor in charge of military matters), in its plural form "Marshals".
details: Writing `[marshals|E]` in a text shows "Marshals" linked to the marshal concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a faith doctrine text about who can be appointed to council positions.

label: Martial
summary: The game concept Martial Skill, under its short name "Martial": how good a character is at waging war and leading armies in battle.
details: Writing `[martial|E]` in a text shows the word "Martial" linked to the martial skill concept's explanation. A high martial skill matters most for army commanders, since it raises their advantage in battle; the matching lifestyle is the martial lifestyle. Vanilla uses it in board game events and building conditions.
